subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should channel-originated sessions keep auto-delivering bare assistant text by default, or should OpenClaw require message-tool/final-only delivery for more source replies to prevent intermediate text leaks?
rationale: The strict path better prevents disclosure of planning/reasoning text, but current docs and tests preserve automatic delivery for compatibility with models and deployments that rely on plain final assistant text.

options.title: Adopt a staged strict policy
options.body: Preserve the least risky direct-chat compatibility path while making shared room/channel or explicit message-tool sessions stricter, with docs and tests for remaining automatic mode.

options.title: Keep automatic defaults with opt-in guards
options.body: Land opt-in final-tag or verbose-off guards and leave the existing automatic bare-text default unchanged for now.

options.title: Switch source replies to strict delivery
options.body: Require message-tool/final-only delivery more broadly and include upgrade notes, doctor/config guidance, and coverage for users who relied on automatic replies.

recommendation.title: Adopt a staged strict policy
recommendation.body: Preserve the least risky direct-chat compatibility path while making shared room/channel or explicit message-tool sessions stricter, with docs and tests for remaining automatic mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is recent ownership of visible-reply defaults and broad agent-runtime delivery boundaries.
